title: Partially isophase electro-magnetic configurations
abstract: Separation of variables in Schrödinger equation allows an infinite-dimensional family of physically distinct field configurations that are dynamically indistinguishable in one selected sector, labeled by a conserved quantum number, while differing in all others. We call such a symmetry a partial isophase symmetry. Two main examples are considered: axially symmetric magnetic backgrounds (a rigid spectral flow of the Fock--Darwin oscillator, purely magnetic isophase families, and a two-channel extension) and a Cartesian slab geometry (magnetic barriers in two-dimensional electron gases, treated in the Appendices). We further discuss the consequences of this symmetry for the inverse spectral problem and consider its quasiclassical counterpart.
summary: This work introduces the concept of 'partial isophase symmetry' to characterize electromagnetic backgrounds that can change while leaving the quantum dynamics invariant in one specific energy sector. By analyzing the Schrödinger equation, the authors demonstrate that such symmetries allow for the construction of infinite families of dynamically equivalent fields. This provides a theoretical framework for understanding protected quantum channels in complex electromagnetic environments.
main_problem: The paper investigates a novel type of invariance, termed 'partial isophase symmetry,' in the quantum dynamics of a charged particle subjected to time-varying electromagnetic fields.
main_result: The symmetry implies the existence of an infinite family of physically distinct, yet dynamically equivalent, electromagnetic backgrounds that leave the quantum evolution invariant in one specific, protected energy sector.
method: The analysis uses the 3D Schrödinger equation, focusing on separation of variables and deriving conditions for Hamiltonian invariance under field deformations, including extensions to two-channel isospectrality.
model_or_system: The system is a charged particle governed by the Schrödinger equation in an external electromagnetic field, analyzed primarily in axially symmetric geometries (e.g., Fock-Darwin oscillator) and generalized to 2DEG slab geometries.
key_observables: Energy spectrum, wave packet evolution, transmission coefficient (T), and the conserved quantum number labeling the protected sector.
important_parameters: The conserved quantum number ($l$), the deformation parameter ($\delta f(ho)$), and the magnetic field components ($\mathbf{B}, \mathbf{E}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on the existence of separation of variables and treats the system in the quasiclassical limit for some derivations.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate spectral flow (linear shifts in energy levels) and the effect of field deformations on classical trajectories, showing invariant quantities along specific curves.
paper_structure: The paper introduces the partial isophase symmetry via separation of variables, analyzes the axially symmetric case (Fock-Darwin), extends the symmetry to multiple channels using Darboux transformations, and discusses the implications for the inverse spectral problem.
why_interesting: The concept of partial isophase symmetry provides a powerful tool for understanding how physical systems can undergo dramatic external changes while maintaining robust, protected quantum dynamics in specific subspaces, which is relevant for designing robust quantum devices.
